paper.title: Combined experimental and simulation study on H2 storage in oxygen and nitrogen co-doped activated carbon derived from biomass waste: superior pore size and surface chemistry development

defaults.verified_by: Agent B: 178 cells verified, all numeric and controlled-vocabulary cells agreed; 1 dispute upheld (KOH:char mass ratio inverted in the 3 N-AC synthesis descriptions, corrected to 2 g KOH per 1 g char); pore_volume_method unspecified dismissed by corpus convention

notes.codope: oxygen and nitrogen co-doped activated carbon; dopant_element=N records the deliberately urea-introduced nitrogen with its elemental-analysis weight percent; the schema holds one dopant, so the oxygen content (reported by mass difference) is kept in the description and functional_groups only
notes.porevol: total_pore_volume_cm3_g is a single-point (Gurvich) value from the N2 amount adsorbed at P/Po = 0.95; the paper tabulates no micropore or mesopore volume and no single average pore diameter (the NLDFT pore-size distribution appears only in Fig 3b, figure-only), so pore_volume_method is unspecified and no pore diameter is recorded
notes.method: H2 capacity measured on a Micromeritics ASAP2020 plus (static volumetric); samples evacuated to ultrahigh vacuum at 300 C for 12 h before measurement; isotherms up to 1 bar between -196 and 25 C; N2/BET degassed 6 h at 300 C; sample mass and blank/calibration not stated
notes.type: uptake_type unspecified (exact-word rule): the paper labels these values only H2 uptake / H2 adsorption capacity; the word excess occurs only on the GCMC graphite-surface validation (Fig 11, Surface excess umol/m2), a different, simulated quantity
notes.littab: Table 1 is a mixed table; only the five present-work samples are extracted, the remaining rows being other authors' literature values (column Year/ref.) and excluded
notes.scope: the title's simulation refers to a separate GCMC study of idealised slit-pore models (Figs 11-14); it is not an uptake of these samples and no simulated value is recorded

S1.label: N-AC900-2
S1.material_description: N-AC900-2: oxygen and nitrogen co-doped activated carbon from jujube (Ziziphus mauritiana) branch biomass; carbonised 600 C, urea air-oxidation (1:1) at 350 C, KOH activation (2 g KOH per 1 g char), CO2 activation at 900 C for 2 h; N 2.79 wt%, O 13.88 wt% by elemental analysis (O by mass difference)
S1.activation_method: urea air-oxidation (urea:char 1:1) at 350 C, then KOH chemical activation (2 g KOH per 1 g char), then CO2 physical activation at 900 C for 2 h
S1.purification_method: washed with hot water until filtrate neutral pH, dried 105 C 24 h
S1.functional_groups: O groups: carbonyl, hydroxyl, carboxyl (FTIR + O 1s XPS); N groups: pyridinic-N (N6), pyrrolic-N (N5), quaternary-N (NQ), pyridinic-N-oxide (Ox-N6) (N 1s XPS); O content 13.88 wt% (elemental analysis)

S2.label: N-AC900-1
S2.material_description: N-AC900-1: oxygen and nitrogen co-doped activated carbon from jujube branch biomass; urea air-oxidation (1:1) 350 C, KOH activation (2 g KOH per 1 g char), CO2 activation at 900 C for 1 h; N 5.34 wt%, O 11.25 wt% by elemental analysis (O by mass difference)
S2.activation_method: urea air-oxidation (urea:char 1:1) at 350 C, then KOH chemical activation (2 g KOH per 1 g char), then CO2 physical activation at 900 C for 1 h
S2.purification_method: washed with hot water until filtrate neutral pH, dried 105 C 24 h
S2.functional_groups: O groups: carbonyl, hydroxyl, carboxyl; N groups: pyridinic-N (N6), pyrrolic-N (N5), quaternary-N (NQ), pyridinic-N-oxide (Ox-N6); O content 11.25 wt% (elemental analysis)

S3.label: N-AC800-1
S3.material_description: N-AC800-1: oxygen and nitrogen co-doped activated carbon from jujube branch biomass; urea air-oxidation (1:1) 350 C, KOH activation (2 g KOH per 1 g char), CO2 activation at 800 C for 1 h; N 6.16 wt%, O 11.51 wt% by elemental analysis (O by mass difference)
S3.activation_method: urea air-oxidation (urea:char 1:1) at 350 C, then KOH chemical activation (2 g KOH per 1 g char), then CO2 physical activation at 800 C for 1 h
S3.purification_method: washed with hot water until filtrate neutral pH, dried 105 C 24 h
S3.functional_groups: O groups: carbonyl, hydroxyl, carboxyl; N groups: pyridinic-N (N6), pyrrolic-N (N5), quaternary-N (NQ), pyridinic-N-oxide (Ox-N6); O content 11.51 wt% (elemental analysis)

S4.label: AC900
S4.material_description: AC900: activated carbon from jujube branch biomass, CO2-activated at 900 C for 1 h; the paper's unmodified base carbon (no urea or KOH doping step); incidental N 1.42 wt%, O 14.10 wt% by elemental analysis from the biomass precursor
S4.activation_method: CO2 physical activation at 900 C for 1 h
S4.functional_groups: incidental O and N from the biomass precursor; O content 14.10 wt%, N 1.42 wt% (elemental analysis)
S4.note_extra: AC900 is the unmodified base carbon; its N and O content is incidental to the biomass precursor rather than a deliberate doping step, so dopant_element is left empty (cf. the oxygen-is-not-a-dopant convention)

S5.label: AC800
S5.material_description: AC800: activated carbon from jujube branch biomass, CO2-activated at 800 C for 1 h; the paper's unmodified base carbon (no urea or KOH doping step); incidental N 1.33 wt%, O 9.68 wt% by elemental analysis from the biomass precursor
S5.activation_method: CO2 physical activation at 800 C for 1 h
S5.functional_groups: incidental O and N from the biomass precursor; O content 9.68 wt%, N 1.33 wt% (elemental analysis)
S5.note_extra: AC800 is the unmodified base carbon; its N and O content is incidental to the biomass precursor rather than a deliberate doping step, so dopant_element is left empty (cf. the oxygen-is-not-a-dopant convention)
